newsitem.title: USA: No more victims expected in Houston wall collapse.
newsitem.headline: No more victims expected in Houston wall collapse.

text.p: Rescue workers do not expect to find anyone else in the rubble from a wall that collapsed on Thursday during renovations of a Houston mall, killing three people, officials said on Friday.

Up to six people were initially believed missing after the wall collapsed on several people walking in the mall for exercise, but Houston Fire Department spokesman Rick Flanagan said crews clearing away the remaining debris do not expect to find more bodies.
"There's been no other body finds," Flanagan said. "It appears that no one else is unaccounted for."

Rescue workers pulled the bodies of three women out of the rubble at the Northline mall north of Houston on Thursday, and 60 rescue workers searched through the debris overnight looking for other possible victims.

The 20-foot-tall (six-metre-tall) wall collapsed as demolition teams were tearing down a vacant department store to make way for a 12-screen movie theater to be built by a company owned by former basketball star Earvin "Magic" Johnson.

Six people were also injured as concrete beams from the roof gave way and a two-story walkway fell on the early morning walkers, officials said. Crews used three large cranes to remove the concrete beams, and planned to shore up an adjacent wall and clear the remaining debris from the site on Friday.

Since the mall opened in March 1963 there have been three other structural collapses, including one three weeks after the mall opened in which a section of roof gave way under the weight of accumulated rainwater. No one was killed or injured in the earlier accidents, the Houston Chronicle reported.
